tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black spots with concentric rings ('target board' pattern), usually starting on older bottom leaves. Leaves yellow and drop prematurely.

organic_measures.name: Copper Hydroxide / Bordeaux Mixture Spray
organic_measures.method: Apply copper-based organic fungicide (1-2 g per liter) thoroughly on both leaf surfaces.
organic_measures.application: Foliar spray during cool morning or evening hours
organic_measures.frequency: Every 7 to 10 days until disease progression halts

organic_measures.name: Bio-fungicide (Trichoderma viride / Bacillus subtilis)
organic_measures.method: Spray Trichoderma viride or Bacillus subtilis formulation (5 g/ml per liter of water) to outcompete fungal spores.

organic_measures.name: Bottom Foliage Sanitation
organic_measures.method: Prune and remove infected lower leaves (up to 12 inches from ground). Dispose of debris away from the field; do not compost infected material.

chemical_measures.name: Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Wear PPE (gloves, mask, goggles). Do not spray during bloom period. Pre-harvest interval (PHI): 7 days.

chemical_measures.name: Chlorothalonil or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Rotate chemical modes of action to prevent fungal resistance. Strict compliance with label instructions required.

prevention_measures: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (avoid potatoes, peppers, eggplants).
Use drip irrigation instead of overhead watering to keep foliage dry.
Apply organic straw or plastic mulch around the plant base to prevent soil-splash onto lower leaves.
Ensure adequate plant spacing (at least 45-60 cm) for good air circulation.
sources: ICAR - Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) Tomato Disease Guide
University of Florida IFAS Extension: Early Blight of Tomato
FAO Integrated Pest Management in Vegetable Production

tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale green to dark brown lesions on leaves and stems, with white velvety fungal growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions.

organic_measures.name: Fixed Copper Compounds
organic_measures.method: Apply copper octanoate or copper oxychloride (2.5 g per liter) immediately upon first suspicion.
organic_measures.frequency: Every 5 to 7 days during cool, wet weather

organic_measures.name: Immediate Roguing of Severely Infected Plants
organic_measures.method: Bag and uproot heavily infected plants during dry weather to prevent rapid airborne spore spread.

chemical_measures.name: Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold 68 WG)
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Systemic and contact action. Wear full PPE. Pre-harvest interval (PHI): 14 days. Avoid overuse to curb resistance.

chemical_measures.name: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb 72% WP
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Apply at early symptom stage. Follow local agrochemical regulations.

prevention_measures: Plant certified disease-free transplants or resistant varieties (e.g., Defiant, Mountain Magic).
Avoid planting tomatoes near potato fields.
Eliminate volunteer tomato and potato plants and weed hosts like nightshade.
Maximize canopy aeration with staking and trellis systems.
sources: Cornell University Vegetable MD Online: Late Blight on Tomato
ICAR - National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM)
European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO) Data Sheets

tomato_bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark brown, water-soaked circular lesions on leaves, often with a yellow halo. Centers may dry out and tear. Fruit may show raised scab-like spots.

organic_measures.name: Copper Soap (Copper Octanoate) + Bacillus amyloliquefaciens
organic_measures.method: Tank-mix biological bactericide (Bacillus amyloliquefaciens) with low-rate copper soap.
organic_measures.frequency: Every 7 days in warm, rainy weather

organic_measures.name: Hot Water Seed Treatment (Prior to planting)
organic_measures.method: Soak seeds at 50°C (122°F) for 25 minutes to eliminate seed-borne bacteria.
organic_measures.application: Seed treatment prior to nursery sowing

chemical_measures.name: Streptomycin Sulphate + Tetracycline Hydrochloride (Agricultural grade) + Copper Oxychloride
chemical_measures.active_ingredient: Streptocycline 90:10 (0.5 g/10 L) + COC 50 WP (2.5 g/L)
chemical_measures.dosage: As per local extension prescription only
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Antibiotic use strictly governed by local agricultural policies. Wear PPE. Do not apply close to harvest.

prevention_measures: Use certified pathogen-free seeds and nursery stock.
Never work in wet fields or handle foliage when leaves are damp to avoid mechanical bacterial transmission.
Disinfect pruning tools with 70% alcohol or 10% bleach solution between rows.
Rotate fields away from solanaceous crops for at least 2 seasons.
sources: University of California Statewide Integrated Pest Management Program (UC IPM)
ICAR-IIHR Tomato Disease Advisory
APS Plant Pathology Compendium of Tomato Diseases

tomato_septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-3 mm) with dark brown margins and sunken grayish-white centers with tiny black dots (pycnidia). Leaves turn yellow and drop from base upward.

organic_measures.name: Copper-based Organic Protectant
organic_measures.method: Foliar spray of copper hydroxide (2 g/L) at the first sign of leaf spotting.

organic_measures.name: Lower Canopy Stripping
organic_measures.method: Prune symptomatic lower leaves promptly to prevent upward splash dispersion.

chemical_measures.name: Chlorothalonil 75% WP or Mancozeb 75% WP
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Contact protectant fungicide. Ensure full leaf coverage. Wear PPE. Follow label PHI.

prevention_measures: Implement drip irrigation or furrow watering to minimize leaf wetness.
Mulch beds heavily to create a physical barrier against soil-borne spores.
Deep plow crop residues after harvest to bury fungal inocula.
Provide wide row spacing for maximum airflow and sun penetration.
sources: Purdue Extension Vegetable Crops Hotline
Penn State Extension: Septoria Leaf Spot on Tomato
ICAR NCIPM Guidelines

tomato_leaf_mold.symptoms: Pale greenish-yellow chlorotic patches on the upper leaf surface, with dense olive-green to brown velvety spore growth on the corresponding lower surface.

organic_measures.name: Potassium Bicarbonate or Bio-fungicide Spray
organic_measures.method: Spray potassium bicarbonate (3 g/L) or Bacillus subtilis (3 ml/L) on leaf undersides.

organic_measures.name: Greenhouse Humidity Reduction
organic_measures.method: Improve ventilation, install exhaust fans, and reduce relative humidity below 85%.

chemical_measures.name: Difenoconazole 25% EC or Azoxystrobin 23% SC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Apply at early symptom emergence. Observe 5-7 days pre-harvest interval.

prevention_measures: Prune suckers and dense foliage to promote rapid air movement through the plant canopy.
Avoid overhead irrigation; water early in the day so foliage dries rapidly.
Grow leaf-mold resistant hybrid varieties in greenhouse or polytunnel setups.
Maintain greenhouse temperatures and adequate venting during cool, foggy mornings.
sources: University of Massachusetts Amherst Greenhouse Crops and Floriculture Program
Ohio State University Extension: Leaf Mold of Tomato
FAO Protective Cultivation Handbook

tomato_spider_mites.symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckling (stippling) on leaves. As infestation progresses, leaves bronze, dry out, and fine silken webbing covers leaf undersides and shoot tips.

organic_measures.name: Neem Oil Extract / Azadirachtin 1% EC
organic_measures.method: Spray cold-pressed neem oil (5 ml/L with soap emulsifier) or Azadirachtin (2 ml/L) thoroughly on leaf undersides.

organic_measures.name: Biological Predatory Mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis)
organic_measures.method: Release beneficial predatory mites in infested patches early before heavy webbing forms.

organic_measures.name: Insecticidal Soap / Horticultural Oil
organic_measures.method: Spray potassium soap solution (5-10 ml/L) directly contacting the mites.

chemical_measures.name: Spiromesifen 22.9% SC or Propargite 57% EC
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Target undersides where mites feed. Alternate miticide classes to avoid rapid resistance development. Wear PPE.

prevention_measures: Keep field borders free of broadleaf weeds that harbor overwintering mite colonies.
Avoid water-stressing tomato plants; drought-stressed plants are significantly more susceptible.
Avoid excessive use of broad-spectrum pyrethroid insecticides which eliminate natural mite predators.
Wash dust off farm roads and field edges as dust promotes spider mite outbreaks.
sources: UC IPM: Tomato Spider Mites Pest Management Guidelines
ICAR-NCIPM Mite Management Protocol
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension

tomato_target_spot.symptoms: Small brown necrotic spots with subtle yellow halos that expand to 5-10 mm circular lesions with light brown centers and dark concentric rings.

organic_measures.name: Copper Hydroxide + Bio-stimulant Spray
organic_measures.method: Apply copper hydroxide (2 g/L) combined with seaweed extract to strengthen plant cell wall resistance.

organic_measures.name: Canopy Airflow Enhancement
organic_measures.method: Prune overcrowded foliage and stake branches firmly off wet ground.

chemical_measures.name: Fluxapyroxad + Pyraclostrobin or Azoxystrobin
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Follow label timing. Rotate with multi-site contact protectants like Chlorothalonil.

prevention_measures: Eliminate solanaceous and cucurbit crop residues after harvest.
Ensure wide plant spacing for sunlight penetration.
Use drip irrigation to maintain dry leaf surfaces.
Implement crop rotation with monocots like corn or sorghum.
sources: University of Florida EDIS: Target Spot of Tomato
ICAR-IIHR Plant Pathology Division
CABI Crop Protection Compendium

tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.pathogen: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (Begomovirus, vectored by Bemisia tabaci Whitefly)
tomato_yellow_leaf_curl_virus.symptoms: Severe plant stunting, erect bushy shoots, cupped and curled leaves with prominent interveinal and marginal yellowing (chlorosis), and flower drop.

organic_measures.name: Yellow Sticky Traps for Whitefly Vector Monitoring
organic_measures.method: Install yellow sticky cards (15-20 traps per acre) at canopy height to trap adult whitefly vectors.

organic_measures.name: Neem / Botanical Insecticide (Azadirachtin)
organic_measures.method: Foliar spray of 1% Azadirachtin (2 ml/L) targeting leaf undersides to repel whiteflies and disrupt nymph molting.
organic_measures.application: Early morning spray on leaf undersides

organic_measures.name: Immediate Roguing of Symptomatic Plants
organic_measures.method: Carefully remove and bag infected plants early to prevent whiteflies from acquiring the virus and spreading it across the field.

chemical_measures.name: Thiamethoxam 25% WG or Acetamiprid 20% SP (Vector management)
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: Note: Chemical controls manage the insect vector (whitefly), NOT the virus itself. Strictly avoid spraying during active honeybee pollination hours. Pre-harvest interval (PHI): 5-7 days.

prevention_measures: Plant TYLCV-resistant or tolerant tomato hybrids (e.g., US 440, Sakata varieties with Ty-1/Ty-3 resistance genes).
Raise seedlings under 40-50 mesh insect-proof nylon net houses to prevent early nursery vector transmission.
Use reflective silver plastic mulch to disorient flying whiteflies and reduce alighting on young transplants.
Maintain a host-free crop-break period between successive tomato seasons.
sources: ICAR-Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR) Whitefly and TYLCV Management
UC Davis IPM: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl
World Vegetable Center (AVRDC) Fact Sheet

tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, leaf distortion or 'fern-leaf' thinning, slight stunting, and internal brown necrosis in fruit.

organic_measures.name: Milk Spray / Protein Solution (Mechanochemical barrier)
organic_measures.method: Spray 20% skimmed milk in water solution on seedlings prior to transplanting/pruning to denature viral particles and reduce mechanical transmission.
organic_measures.application: Foliar contact spray before handling plants

organic_measures.name: Sanitation with Trisodium Phosphate (TSP) / Soap
organic_measures.method: Wash hands and dip pruning tools in 10% Trisodium Phosphate (TSP) solution or soapy water before touching healthy plants.

organic_measures.name: Roguing and Disposal
organic_measures.method: Carefully pull out infected plants, bag them, and destroy away from the field. Do not burn or compost.

chemical_measures.name: No Chemical Cure Available
chemical_measures.safety_precautions: There are no synthetic chemical viricides for plant viruses. Chemical pesticide sprays are ineffective against ToMV and should not be used.

prevention_measures: Use certified virus-free seeds treated with heat (70°C for 3 days) or TSP.
Grow ToMV-resistant cultivars (designated with 'T' or 'ToMV' resistance on seed packets).
Enforce strict field hygiene: prohibit tobacco smoking/handling near plants (tobacco mosaic virus can cross-contaminate).
Avoid handling plants when leaves are wet.
sources: University of California IPM: Tomato Mosaic Virus
ICAR-IIVR Solanaceous Crop Virus Guide
Cornell Vegetable Pathology Series

tomato_healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green uniform foliage, strong stem growth, normal flowering and fruit set with no visible lesions, wilting, mosaic, or insect damage.

organic_measures.name: Preventive Bio-fertilizer & Micro-nutrient Boost
organic_measures.method: Apply balanced compost tea, Panchagavya (3% foliar spray), or seaweed extract to maintain robust plant vigor and natural immunity.

organic_measures.name: Routine Monitoring
organic_measures.method: Continue weekly inspection of lower leaves, stems, and leaf undersides for early pest presence.

prevention_measures: Maintain consistent soil moisture using drip irrigation; avoid drought cycles to prevent blossom end rot.
Ensure balanced N-P-K fertilization with adequate calcium and potassium.
Keep staking and trellis structures clean and secure.
Maintain clean field borders to discourage weed hosts.
sources: ICAR Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Tomato
FAO Tomato Production Manual
